note: Statements are paraphrases written for this project, not guideline text. Each card names the rubric fact that pulls it into context, so retrieval is deterministic and every citation an agent makes can be checked against this file.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Section 8
cards.topic: Who is eligible for obesity pharmacotherapy
cards.statement: Medicines for obesity are approved as an addition to reduced-calorie eating and more physical activity for adults with a BMI of 30 or above, or 27 or above when at least one weight-related condition is also present. Examples of qualifying conditions include type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and abnormal lipids.

cards.source: ADA Obesity Association 2026, Pharmacologic Treatment of Obesity in Adults
cards.topic: Medicine sits on top of behavioural care, not instead of it
cards.statement: Prescribe obesity medicines only alongside behavioural and lifestyle treatment, and complete a full pre-treatment review first: weight history, weight-related conditions, examination and relevant labs.

cards.source: ADA Obesity Association 2026, Pharmacologic Treatment of Obesity in Adults
cards.topic: Check the current medicine list for drugs that add weight
cards.statement: Before starting an obesity medicine, review what else the patient takes. Drugs that promote weight gain are common, and the more of them a patient is on, the more their BMI and waist tend to rise over time. Consider switching to alternatives that do not add weight.

cards.source: AACE 2025 obesity / ABCD algorithm
cards.citation: Nadolsky K, et al. Endocr Pract. 2025;31(11):1351-1394
cards.topic: Stage the disease by complications, not by BMI alone
cards.statement: Stage 1 means no current weight-related conditions but future risk. Stage 2 means mild to moderate complications. Stage 3 means at least one severe complication. Staging is largely independent of BMI: if complications are present, the amount of body fat is already harming health whether the BMI is 28 or 38.

cards.source: AACE 2025 obesity / ABCD algorithm
cards.citation: Nadolsky K, et al. Endocr Pract. 2025;31(11):1351-1394
cards.topic: Treat harder once complications appear
cards.statement: Treatment intensity should follow the stage. Once complications are present the goal shifts to reversing them, which usually means using medicine rather than relying on lifestyle change alone. The target is better health, not a number on the scale.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Recommendation 9.7
cards.topic: Type 2 diabetes with established or high-risk cardiovascular disease
cards.statement: For adults with type 2 diabetes and established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, or at high risk of it, the treatment plan should include a medicine shown to reduce cardiovascular events, such as a GLP-1 receptor agonist or an SGLT2 inhibitor. This holds regardless of the current HbA1c.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Recommendation 9.10
cards.topic: Type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease
cards.statement: For adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, meaning a confirmed eGFR between 20 and 60 or albuminuria, use an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven benefit in this group. The aim is to slow kidney decline and cut cardiovascular events as well as manage glucose, and it applies regardless of HbA1c.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Recommendations 9.8 and 9.9
cards.topic: Type 2 diabetes with heart failure
cards.statement: For type 2 diabetes with heart failure of either type, an SGLT2 inhibitor is recommended for glucose control and to prevent heart failure admissions, regardless of HbA1c. Where obesity and symptomatic HFpEF are both present, the plan should include an incretin-based medicine shown to improve heart failure symptoms or reduce events.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026
cards.topic: HbA1c is no longer the only measure of success
cards.statement: Cutting cardiovascular and kidney risk now sits alongside glucose control as a primary goal, not below it. Do not treat HbA1c as the sole marker of whether treatment is working.

cards.source: US prescribing information, semaglutide and tirzepatide
cards.citation: WEGOVY and ZEPBOUND prescribing information, boxed warning
cards.topic: Absolute contraindication: thyroid C-cell tumour risk
cards.statement: These medicines carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumours and must not be used in anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or in anyone with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2. The warning applies to the whole class. A family history of papillary, follicular or Hurthle cell thyroid cancer is not a contraindication.

cards.source: US prescribing information, semaglutide and tirzepatide
cards.topic: Absolute contraindication: prior serious reaction
cards.statement: Do not use in anyone who has had a serious hypersensitivity reaction to the drug or any of its ingredients. Anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported after marketing.

cards.source: ADA Obesity Association 2026, Pharmacologic Treatment of Obesity in Adults
cards.topic: Absolute contraindication: pregnancy
cards.statement: Obesity medicines are contraindicated in pregnancy. For anyone who is pregnant or planning a pregnancy, step up lifestyle treatment instead. Stop the medicine when a pregnancy is recognised.

cards.source: US prescribing information, GLP-1 receptor agonist class
cards.citation: WEGOVY prescribing information, warnings and precautions
cards.topic: Caution: pancreatitis
cards.statement: Acute pancreatitis has been seen with these medicines. Stop the drug promptly if it is suspected. A past episode calls for a careful discussion rather than an automatic no.

cards.source: US prescribing information, GLP-1 receptor agonist class
cards.citation: WEGOVY prescribing information, warnings and precautions
cards.topic: Caution: severe stomach emptying problems
cards.statement: These medicines slow stomach emptying. Severe gastroparesis is a reason to avoid them or to be very cautious. Patients should tell any anaesthetist about the medicine before surgery or sedation because of aspiration risk.

cards.source: US prescribing information, GLP-1 receptor agonist class
cards.citation: WEGOVY prescribing information, warnings and precautions
cards.topic: Caution: gallbladder disease
cards.statement: Gallbladder problems including stones have been reported, more often with faster or larger weight loss. Active gallbladder disease calls for caution rather than an automatic no.

cards.source: US prescribing information, semaglutide
cards.topic: Caution: diabetic eye disease
cards.statement: Rapid improvement in glucose control can temporarily worsen diabetic retinopathy. Check eye status before starting in anyone with diabetes and a history of retinopathy, and monitor. Mild or moderate non-proliferative changes are not a contraindication.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Section 8
cards.topic: The best dose is not always the highest dose
cards.statement: Individualise the dose and how fast you step it up, balancing how well it works against how well it is tolerated. The best dose for a given patient may be below the maximum approved one.

cards.source: GLP-1 receptor agonist prescribing information and pooled trial analyses
cards.citation: Semaglutide prescribing information; SUSTAIN and PIONEER pooled analyses
cards.topic: Kidney function and dosing
cards.statement: No dose adjustment is needed for reduced kidney function within the usual treated range. Glucose lowering is similar across eGFR strata. The practical concern is dehydration from nausea or vomiting, especially alongside a diuretic, an SGLT2 inhibitor or a renin-angiotensin blocker.

cards.source: GLP-1 receptor agonist prescribing information, renal impairment warning
cards.citation: OZEMPIC prescribing information, warnings and precautions
cards.topic: Sick-day risk when combined with other kidney-active drugs
cards.statement: Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea cause fluid loss and have led to acute kidney injury. Risk is higher alongside an SGLT2 inhibitor and a renin-angiotensin blocker. Step the dose up slowly and give clear sick-day instructions.

cards.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Section 8
cards.topic: How much weight loss is worth aiming for
cards.statement: Losing 5 to 7 percent of body weight improves glucose and other cardiovascular risk markers. Anyone losing weight on purpose should be told to keep protein and micronutrient intake adequate.

cards.source: AACE 2025 obesity / ABCD algorithm
cards.citation: Nadolsky K, et al. Endocr Pract. 2025;31(11):1351-1394
cards.topic: Overweight without complications
cards.statement: Where there is excess weight but no current weight-related condition, the aim is risk reduction through lifestyle change. This sits at the preclinical end of the spectrum and does not by itself call for drug treatment.

cards.source: AACE 2025 obesity / ABCD algorithm; ADA Obesity Association 2026
cards.citation: Endocr Pract. 2025;31(11):1351-1394; Diabetes Obes Cardiometab Care. 2026;1(1):5-36
cards.topic: What to do when the incretin class is closed off
cards.statement: A contraindication to one class does not mean no treatment. Other approved long-term options exist that do not act on the incretin pathway, and metabolic surgery remains on the table for patients whose BMI and complications support it.
